# n8n: MCP OAuth client connection

`n8n-3` · OAuth · person. An MCP client (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc.) runs an OAuth flow; the user approves it in n8n and the client gets the permissions granted at consent.

Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant. "No docs found" means vendor documentation does not say either way.

| Question | Answer | Why | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identify: Admin can list all of them | Yes | Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > View all, all-users view lists every connected OAuth client. | Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > View all, all-users view lists every connected OAuth client. |
| Protect: Admin can block or require approval | Yes | Enable/Disable MCP access; N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp | Enable/Disable MCP access: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connection details · N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp: Environment variable |
| Protect: SSO and MFA rules apply | No docs found | No vendor documentation found. |  |
| Protect: IP restriction | Conditional | Not documented. | Allowed callback URLs: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Access > Allowed callback URLs |
| Protect: Expires automatically | No docs found | Not documented |  |
| Detect: Usage appears in logs | Yes | clientId | Where: Settings > Log Streaming > Add new destination > Events: n8n.audit.mcp; filter authType=oauth, group by clientId |
| Detect: Data reads appear in logs | Conditional | Log streaming is Enterprise only; MCP audit events from n8n 2.34.0. | Where: Settings > Log Streaming > Events: n8n.audit.mcp; filter event n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called with authType=oauth and clientId |
| Respond: Revocation ends active access | Yes | Client is disconnected at once. | Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > Revoke access (all-users view for others). |
| Respond: Stops working when user is removed | No docs found | No vendor documentation found. |  |

## Protect: what an admin can configure

### Admin controls
- **Enable/Disable MCP access** (Disable; all plans; default off). Turns the instance MCP server on or off; disabling disconnects every client. Where: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connection details.
- **N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp** (Disable; Self-hosted only; default off). Removes MCP endpoints entirely. Where: Environment variable.
- **Per-workflow MCP access** (Limit resources; all plans; default off). Only workflows marked Available in MCP can be read in full, run or edited. Where: Workflow settings > Available in MCP; Settings > Instance-level MCP > Workflows enabled.
- **Allowed callback URLs** (Limit network; all plans; default off). Restricts which redirect URLs can finish an MCP OAuth sign-in. Where: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Access > Allowed callback URLs.

### Not available (vendor states)
- No admin approval step for MCP OAuth clients; any signed-in user can approve one while MCP is on.

- Network: unknown (checked at unknown). Not documented.
- Lifetime: Not documented. Renewal: Log docs mention the client's token refreshes; lifetimes are not documented.
- Keyless option: not_applicable. User OAuth consent, not workload federation.
- Conditions: No per-client admin approval.

## Detect: what gets logged
- Token prefix: not established

### Logs
- Log streaming: n8n.audit.mcp.*: Enterprise; from n8n 2.34.0.

### Fields that identify the credential
- `clientId` (n8n.audit.mcp.oauth.completed, n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called): Stable per client registration.

### Lifecycle events
- create: `n8n.audit.mcp.oauth.completed` userId, clientId, clientName.
- use: `n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called` 

### Correlate on
`clientId`, `userId`

### API calls a holder can make, and whether they are logged
- discovery (bulk): `MCP tool search_workflows`. Workflow previews Logged: yes (`n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called`). clientId present
- collection: `MCP tool search_workflows`. Previews of every workflow the user can view Logged: plan (`n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called`). Log streaming is Enterprise only; MCP audit events from n8n 2.34.0.

### What to look for (analyst guidance)
- New clientName not in approved list
- Callback URL mode left at All callback URLs

## Respond: how to revoke it
- Admin: **Revoke access (connected clients)**. Disconnects an OAuth MCP client immediately. Where: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > Revoke access.

Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > Revoke access (all-users view for others). Live access ends on revocation: yes. Client is disconnected at once.
